name: Somany Ceramics Ltd
title: Somany Ceramics Ltd - 531548 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

read.thesis: Somany Q2 FY27 margin rose to 11.7% on utilisation and full price pass-through, but volume only ~5.5% and FY27 guidance trimmed to margin +2–2.5pp; Morbi export shutdowns support domestic supply discipline.

summary.headline: Somany Ceramics Q2 FY27 revenue up ~25% to Rs 154 crore-equivalent tile growth, EBITDA margin 11.7%, FY27 margin guidance raised to +2-2.5pp.
summary.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 revenue growth of roughly 25% with volume up about 5.5%, and EBITDA margin of 11.7% helped by better plant utilisation, full pass-through of price increases and a richer product mix. Tiles grew about 27% and bathware about 18%, while building solutions grew about 28%. Joint ventures swung from a Rs 12 crore loss in Q2 FY26 to a Rs 3 crore profit in Q2 FY27. Management raised its FY27 EBITDA margin improvement guidance to 2-2.5 percentage points over FY26 from 1-1.5 percentage points, and kept high-single-digit revenue growth guidance; bathware is guided to grow about 20%.

financial_highlights.value: ~25% YoY, stated as Rs 154 crore-level figure in transcript (unclear)

financial_highlights.change: Improved YoY, driven by utilisation, pass-through and mix

financial_highlights.value: Profit of Rs 3 crore; Rs 6 crore profit in H1
financial_highlights.change: vs Rs 12 crore loss in Q2 FY26 and Rs 23 crore loss in H1 FY26
vs Rs 43 in Q2 FY26 and Rs 45 average FY26

segments.name: Tiles
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 723 crore, up ~27% YoY; GVT share of mix about 45% vs 41% a year earlier. Management expects tiles to grow about 20% for FY27 and the next year.

segments.name: Bathware
segments.commentary: Grew ~15-18% YoY to about Rs 88 crore in Q2; brass-linked margin pressure in Q1 eased in Q2, with management guiding bathware margins roughly flat to tiles.

segments.name: Building solutions
segments.commentary: Revenue about Rs 45 crore, up ~28% YoY; now ~16-17% of revenue, with a new north plant started in October and a south plant started in Q2, targeting 20-25% of revenue in 2-3 years.

segments.name: Joint ventures
segments.commentary: Turned to Rs 3 crore profit in Q2 from Rs 12 crore loss a year ago; management reiterated a swing of at least Rs 40 crore for FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at high single digits, which management is confident of achieving.

FY27 EBITDA margin improvement over FY26 revised to ~2-2.5 percentage points from earlier 1-1.5 percentage points; FY27 margin now guided around 11.5% and management expects FY28 to be higher, above 11.5-12%.
Bathware growth guided at ~20% for FY27.
Marketing spend held at ~2% of revenue for the full year, with absolute spend significantly higher than last year.
Q3 volumes expected better than Q2 in absolute terms; Q4 expected significantly better as upgraded plants return.
Capacity addition of ~4 million sq m annualised in FY27 with ~10-11 million sq m more next year; expansion in south (Ceravet) to add ~11-12 million sq m, commissioning around September 2027.
risks_watch: Gas price volatility (LPG/propane/natural gas) linked to geopolitical conflict; current ~Rs 70 per SCM vs Rs 45 in FY26.
Morbi export shutdowns and any new geopolitical disruption affecting pricing and competitive dynamics.
Brass cost inflation (roughly doubled in 1.5 years) not fully passed through in bathware.
Execution of the Q3-Q4 volume ramp after plant upgrades, and commissioning of the south expansion by around September 2027.
Management's FY27 targets (margin 2-2.5pp improvement, high-single-digit growth) depend on continued gas pass-through and export recovery in Morbi.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company hold the price increases of the last two quarters if gas prices correct?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gas has corrected only slightly since April and the 16-17% price increase since April has been fully passed through; gas is holding at about Rs 70, and it expects Rs 70-71 barring a major shock.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company affected by Morbi export disruption and geopolitical developments?
qa_highlights.answer: About 45% of Morbi is shut with another 10% expected over Diwali; exports should improve in November and restart in January. The company does not export much, so it was not hit; a possible US ban on Chinese-made engineered tiles could open export opportunities.

qa_highlights.question: What GBT mix is targeted and will it expand margins?
qa_highlights.answer: GBT is about 45% vs about 40% last year, rising toward 65-70% in 2-3 years as new capacity is all GBT; management said GBT gives only slightly better margins, and guided FY27 margin expansion of 2-2.5pp.

qa_highlights.question: What are the capex and JV plans, including Nepal JV and CeraVet?
qa_highlights.answer: Stake in the Nepal JV to rise to 76% from 51%; CeraVet expansion to add 11-12 million sq m at total cost about Rs 150 crore with Rs 60 crore equity share; Sudha Rs 15 crore and Vintage Rs 8 crore modernisation; routine capex about Rs 72 crore funded internally.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current capacity utilisation and gas price level at which production becomes unviable?
qa_highlights.answer: Running plants at 100% utilisation, with only planned upgrade downtime of 15-20 days in July-August. Management sees no threat of substitution even if tile prices rise 50%.

qa_highlights.question: Why was volume growth only ~5% and when will it reach double digits?
qa_highlights.answer: Plant maintenance and upgrades cut volume; management said it could have delivered 1-1.5pp more volume. Q3 volume expected slightly above Q2 and Q4 significantly better; volume growth guided to 7-8% in the next quarter or two.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q3 seasonality of low volume and margin reverse this year, and what is the margin outlook beyond FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects Q3 volume to be better than Q2 with no disruption; FY27 margin guided around 11.5%, with FY28 expected above 11.5-12% from capacity additions, JV swing of about Rs 40 crore and the better mix.

qa_highlights.question: How is the bathware margin trend and pass-through of brass costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Bathware margins are a couple of points above tiles; most gas-related price hikes were passed on, but brass (doubled in 1.5 years) was only partly passed on. Q1 was a drag; Q2 was better than Q1, and margins expected to be about the same as tiles.

capex_capacity: Annualised capacity to rise by about 4 million sq m in FY27 from plant upgrades and debottlenecking within existing plants; about 10-11 million sq m more capacity next year (FY28).
South JV (CeraVet) expansion to add about 11-12 million sq m, up from the earlier announced 9 million sq m; commissioning targeted around September 2027.

Capex: CeraVet expansion total about Rs 150 crore, funded 50% via equity, with Somany's share about Rs 60 crore; buying stake in Nepal JV from 51% to 76%; Rs 15 crore modernisation at Sudha and Rs 8 crore at Vintage; routine capex about Rs 72 crore funded internally.

Upgrades: a north plant line upgrade in October to cut cost and raise capacity, plus a Vintage upgrade in Q1/Q2; plants were down about 15-20 days in July-August. Management expects no volume disruption in Q3.

Building solutions: a large north plant started in October; south plant started in Q2. GVT share of tiles mix about 45% (from 41%), expected to rise further as all new capacity is GVT, with GBT targeted at 65-70% in 2-3 years from about 45%.
demand_pricing: Domestic demand described as decent and resilient across retail and projects in Q2; tiles up ~27% YoY to Rs 723 crore, bathware ~15-18% to Rs 88 crore, building solutions ~28% to about Rs 45 crore.

Industry exports down ~31.2% in first five months of FY27 by value and ~44-45% by volume; FY27 industry exports seen at Rs 12,000-13,000 crore vs Rs 18,750 crore in FY26. Exports improving since October as rates fall.
About 45% of Morbi capacity shut currently, with another ~10% expected shut over Diwali; export restart expected only in January due to European shutdown in December.
Gas blended cost ~Rs 70/SCM vs Rs 43 in Q2 FY26 and Rs 45 average FY26; fully passed through 16-17% price hikes since April; management says prices should hold at ~Rs 70-71 barring a major shock.

Realisations: project channel realisation about 1-1.5pp lower than retail channel; projects ~76% of mix vs retail ~80.5% earlier, per management. Bathware brass costs roughly doubled in 1.5 years, only partly passed through.
Management sees Morbi capacity constrained for 18-24 months given higher land, power and euro-rupee costs, supporting organised players' pricing.
key_quotes: As you would have seen the results, we have grown by approximately 25 percent and the volume stands at 5.5 percent for the quarter.
We have been able to control the overall pricing at approximately 70 rupees standard cubic meter, which is up from 45 rupees of standard cubic meter for FY26
The guidance for the entire year FY27 remains to be high single digits and we are quite sure that we will be able to achieve that.
We are revising that to approximately 2 to 2.5% improvement over the FY26 figures.
So I believe in the next two to three years GBT would become close to 65 to 70%.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on volumes, margins and the expansion pipeline, with explicit comfort on the FY27 high-single-digit growth and margin guidance. Cautious on gas and geopolitical risk, repeatedly saying outcomes depend on how gas and input costs evolve in H2.

adds.what: ~4 million sq m annualised capacity added in FY27 via plant upgrades and debottlenecking within existing plants
~10-11 million sq m more annualised capacity in FY28
CeraVet south JV expansion ~11-12 million sq m (up from earlier 9 million sq m), commissioning ~September 2027
North building solutions plant started October 2026
South building solutions plant started Q2 FY27

growth.why: Management guides high-single-digit FY27 revenue growth (~8% midpoint) and bathware ~20%, backed partly by ~4 mn sq m FY27 debottlenecking, ~11-12 mn sq m CeraVet expansion commissioning ~Sep 2027, and pass-through pricing; Q2 revenue up ~25% YoY, but Morbi shutdowns and export weakness temper near-term visibility.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: FY27 EBITDA margin guided up 2-2.5pp over FY26 to ~11.5% (from 1-1.5pp), with Q2 margin at 11.7% on utilisation, full pass-through of 16-17% gas-led price hikes, and JV swing of at least Rs 40 crore; FY28 guided above 11.5-12%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: ~4 mn sq m annualised added in FY27 via upgrades and debottlenecking, ~10-11 mn sq m more in FY28, and CeraVet expansion of 11-12 mn sq m (Rs 150 crore total) commissioning around September 2027; north building solutions plant started October 2026 and south plant in Q2 FY27.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.when: Q3 FY27 onward; Q4 significantly better
rows.why: Volume grew only ~5.5% in Q2 due to upgrade downtime of 15-20 days (management says 1-1.5pp more was possible); Q3 guided above Q2 and Q4 significantly better, with 7-8% volume growth guided over the next quarter or two.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Plants run at 100% utilisation with only planned downtime, and capex is already committed: CeraVet ~Rs 150 crore (Somany share ~Rs 60 crore), Nepal JV stake to 76% from 51%, Sudha Rs 15 crore and Vintage Rs 8 crore modernisation, routine capex ~Rs 72 crore.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 margin guidance was just raised to 2-2.5pp, and revenue guidance of high-single-digit growth is held; a further raise depends on Q3-Q4 volume ramp and gas staying at ~Rs 70-71 per SCM, with Q2 revenue up ~25% YoY.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Morbi shutdown (~45% shut, another ~10% over Diwali) and export down ~31% by value in first five months of FY27 could weigh on pricing, and gas (~Rs 70 vs Rs 43 a year ago) is a geopolitical risk; management says the targets depend on gas and export recovery.

rows.label: Nepal JV stake rise to 76% from 51%
rows.why: Stake purchase is stated as planned, lifting consolidation control of the Nepal JV from 51% to 76%.

rows.label: Building solutions mix to 20-25% of revenue
rows.why: Building solutions already ~16-17% of revenue (Rs 45 crore, up ~28%) with north and south plants started in Q2-Q3 FY27, targeting 20-25% in 2-3 years.

rows.label: Possible US ban on Chinese engineered tiles
rows.why: Management said a possible US ban could open export opportunities for Indian makers, but the company does not export much and it is conditional on policy.

tone.note: Management was confident on volume ramp, FY27 margin raise and the expansion pipeline, and cautious on gas and geopolitical risk; analysts pressed on gas pass-through durability, Morbi export disruption, and why volume grew only ~5%.
